tools.name: read
tools.title: Read files and folders
tools.description: Read what is at one or more paths. A folder is listed one level deep, a text file comes back as numbered lines, a PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP comes back as an image, and anything else returns its metadata and why it was not decoded. Paths may contain * ? and ** and are expanded here. Every result starts with a header giving size, timestamps and line count. The line-number prefix is display metadata, not file content — strip it before quoting text into apply_patch. start_line/end_line apply to every file the call resolves to; a path may instead carry its own range as path:12-40 or path:12, so several ranges of one file fit in one call. A typical 1,500-line source file fits in the default read: do not pre-paginate it. Batch related paths in one call; only continue from a line when the returned header says more lines follow. Text is bounded at about 512.0 KB; images have a separate 4-image, 12.0 MB base64 budget and view_image's per-file validation.

paths.description: Paths inside the live approved roots: /project, /skills. A root is an approved folder, usually a parent of the project rather than the project itself, so name every folder between the root and the file — the same path exec_command takes as workdir. Reading a root lists it one level deep. Absolute native paths copied from command output are also accepted when they resolve inside one of these roots; globs work in either spelling.

start_line.description: First line, 1-based. Applied to every file the call reads, so prefer one path when the range is file-specific.

end_line.description: Last line, inclusive. Applied to every file the call reads, so prefer one path when the range is file-specific.

max_bytes.description: Per-text-file payload cap. Default 256.0 KB; maximum 512.0 KB. Omit it for ordinary source files.

tools.name: view_image
tools.description: View a local image file from the filesystem when visual inspection is needed. Use this for images already available on disk.

path.description: Local filesystem path to an image file.

tools.name: save_image
tools.description: Save the original file of an image ChatGPT generated in this chat (not a screenshot or preview) to a new file in an approved folder. Never replaces an existing file. The chat must be open in the browser with the image on its page.

path.description: New file path in an approved folder, for example /workspace/images/logo.png. Without an extension the image's own (.png, .jpg or .webp) is added.

nth.description: Which image, counting back from the newest generated in this chat: 1 (the default) is the latest, 2 the one before, and so on.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description:
The `apply_patch` tool can be used to edit files. Pass the patch text as the `patch` string; everything else about the format below is unchanged.

Within each Update File block, put edits in file order. Quote the current file text for old/context lines; matching searches forward and does not reconstruct reformatted code. On a mismatch, use the diagnostic to correct the patch before retrying.

The patch must match this grammar:

start: begin_patch hunk+ end_patch
begin_patch: "*** Begin Patch" LF
end_patch: "*** End Patch" LF?

hunk: add_hunk | delete_hunk | update_hunk
add_hunk: "*** Add File: " filename LF add_line+
delete_hunk: "*** Delete File: " filename LF
update_hunk: "*** Update File: " filename LF change_move? change?

filename: /(.+)/
add_line: "+" /(.*)/ LF -> line

change_move: "*** Move to: " filename LF
change: (change_context | change_line)+ eof_line?
change_context: ("@@" | "@@ " /(.+)/) LF
change_line: ("+" | "-" | " ") /(.*)/ LF
eof_line: "*** End of File" LF

%import common.LF

patch.description: The patch text, from *** Begin Patch through *** End Patch, exactly as the grammar describes it.

tools.name: exec_command
tools.description:
Runs a command and returns output or a session ID. Use write_stdin for progress, input, or retained output. Background results also arrive on later responses.

Windows shell notes:
- Deleting or moving files works reliably inside one shell. Paths listed in PowerShell and handed to `cmd /c`, batch builtins, or another shell for deletion or moving break on quoting; use native PowerShell cmdlets such as `Remove-Item` / `Move-Item` with `-LiteralPath` rather than string-built shell commands.
- Before a recursive delete or move, resolve the absolute target paths and check that they lie inside the intended workspace or the explicitly named target directory, in particular when a path was computed.
- `Start-Process` for a background helper or service: add `-WindowStyle Hidden` unless the user asked for a visible window. Visible windows are for interactive tools the user needs to see or control.

Browsers: do not spawn a new browser, profile or debug port per attempt — each stays resident and heats the CPU. Keep to one or two windows you actually use and reuse the one already open.

cmd.description: Shell command to execute. To read a file, use the read tool instead. This shell is Windows PowerShell 5.1, which has no && or ||: use the cmds array for a sequence, or A; if ($?) { B }.

cmds.description: Use cmd or cmds, not both. cmds runs sequentially in one shell session; sections show exit codes. It continues after ordinary non-zero exits; first non-zero exit wins.

workdir.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the turn cwd.

tty.description: True allocates a PTY for the command; false or omitted uses plain pipes.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait up to 10000 ms (250-30000 on Windows). Finished commands return immediately; otherwise return a session ID.

max_output_tokens.description: Ignored; still accepted so older cached schemas keep working. Omit it.

shell.description: Shell binary to launch. Defaults to the user's default shell.

login.description: True loads the shell profile; false disables it. Defaults to false on Windows for deterministic commands.

exit_code.description: Process exit code when the command finished during this call.

completed_session_id.description: Use as write_stdin session_id to reread completed output.

expected_exit.description: Non-zero exit is an expected result, not a failure.

output_replayed.description: Retained output; command was not run again.

original_token_count.description: Approximate token count before output truncation.

tools.name: write_stdin
tools.description: Polls or writes to the returned session ID. Empty chars reread retained output after completion, including automatic delivery; never reruns work. Completed processes reject input. Retains the latest 64 results in this app, 256 KiB each.

session_id.description: Returned running or completed session ID.

chars.description: Bytes to write to stdin. Defaults to empty, which polls without writing.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding output. Non-empty writes default to 250 ms and cap at 30000 ms; empty polls wait up to 5000-300000 ms by default but return early when the first output arrives.

max_output_tokens.description: Ignored; still accepted so older cached schemas keep working. Omit it.

exit_code.description: Process exit code when the command finished during this call.

completed_session_id.description: Use as write_stdin session_id to reread completed output.

expected_exit.description: Non-zero exit is an expected result, not a failure.

output_replayed.description: Retained output; command was not run again.

original_token_count.description: Approximate token count before output truncation.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.title: Update plan
tools.description: Updates your task plan in the user’s app. Use for work with several meaningful steps; skip simple tasks. Send the complete plan with short step headlines, useful details and current statuses. Keep at most one step in_progress. Update after completing a step or changing approach. This only displays a plan; it does not execute steps or advance queued stages.

explanation.description: Brief explanation of a changed plan.

step.description: Short headline shown to the user.

details.description: Concrete approach, checks or remaining work beneath this headline. Keep useful detail when updating status.

plan.description: The complete updated plan. Send an empty array to clear it.

tools.name: exec
tools.title: Run JavaScript
tools.description: Run JavaScript to compose this connector’s tools. Argument: {code: "raw JavaScript"}; the host chooses the outer namespace. Inside code, use await tools.<tool_name>(args), await Promise.all([...]), text(value), and image(dataUrlOrMcpImageContent). tools return their normal MCP result objects, including content and isError. Only explicit text/image output reaches the model; intermediate results stay in the runtime and local tool recording. ALL_TOOLS lists {name,description}; use the individual tools’ schemas for arguments. Fresh isolated JavaScript runtime, top-level await, no Node, filesystem, network, console or imports. Requires exact companion chat/session identity or Allow unattributed calls enabled. Limits: 64k source characters, 32 MiB JS memory, 2s active JS time, 60s total, 32 calls, 8 concurrent calls, 40k text bytes, 4 images, 12 MiB emitted payload. Await every call. Termination stops JavaScript/new calls, not actions already dispatched. Individual tools remain available. session_finish and agents action=finish must be direct calls. No recursive exec, pragma, wait/yield or persistent globals. See the connector instructions for examples.

code.description: Raw JavaScript source with top-level await. Emit results with text(...) or image(...).
